cards.explanation: The answer is to be gracious to them. Isaiah 30:18 says, “Therefore the LORD longs to be gracious to you…” Longs, friends. That's a long way from putting up with them. After all that running and refusing, I think that word is a soft place to land.

The answer is all who wait for Him. The verse ends, “Blessed are all who wait for Him.” (Isaiah 30:18) Waiting is hard work, friends. I've stared at a timer with nine minutes left like it was telling me fibs. Still, the blessing goes to the ones who wait.

The answer is False. Isaiah 30:19 says, “He will surely be gracious when you cry for help; when He hears, He will answer you.” He hears and He answers. And the verse also says the people will weep no more.

The answer is that He will no longer hide Himself. Isaiah 30:20 says, “…your Teacher will no longer hide Himself…” And the people will see Him with their own eyes. The bread of adversity and the water of affliction come, but the Teacher is seen right there in it.

The answer is behind them. Isaiah 30:21 says, “…your ears will hear this command behind you…” Turn right, turn left, the voice is still back there. Some of us will take any help we can get from behind, friends, especially when we're SURE we know where we're going.

The answer is to throw them away. Isaiah 30:22 says, “You will throw them away…” All that silver-plating and gold-plating, and the people tell those idols, “Be gone!” Shiny doesn't mean it stays on the shelf, friends.

The answer is rain, friends. Isaiah 30:23 says, “Then He will send rain for the seed that you have sown in the ground…” A seed with no rain is just a very patient pebble. This time the rain comes to it.

The answer is True, friends. Isaiah 30:23 says the food that comes from the land “…will be rich and plentiful.” I bake by the batch, and even I'd call that a lot. The cattle graze in open pastures that same day.

The answer is every high mountain and raised hill. Isaiah 30:25 says, “And from every high mountain and every raised hill, streams of water will flow…” Water usually collects down low, friends. Here it's flowing from the high places, every one of them.

The answer is heals, friends. Isaiah 30:26 says it's “…the day that the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wounds He has inflicted.” Binds up and heals, both on that day. And the moon shines like the sun.
The answer is False. Isaiah 30:28 says He comes “…to sift the nations in a sieve of destruction…” The sieve is for the nations, friends. Then the prophet turns back to His people, and they sing.

The answer is that they will sing as on a holy festival night. Isaiah 30:29 says, “You will sing as on the night of a holy festival…” Their heart rejoices like one who walks to the music of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD. After all that fire and smoke in the verses before, singing is the sound that follows for His people.

The answer is fire and hailstones. Isaiah 30:30 says His arm is revealed “…striking in angry wrath with a flame of consuming fire, and with cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.” That's a heavy picture, friends, so I'll just let the verse say it. Fire and hailstones are both right there in it.

The answer is that it will be shattered. Isaiah 30:31 says, “For Assyria will be shattered at the voice of the LORD…” Not a whisper of negotiation, friends. It's shattered at His voice, and He strikes them with His scepter.

The answer is True, friends. Isaiah 30:32 says that with every stroke of the rod, “…the tambourines and lyres will sound…” So there's music playing along with every stroke. Tambourines and lyres together, that's a whole band.

The answer is breath, friends. Isaiah 30:33 says, “The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of burning sulfur, sets it ablaze.” This is a heavy part of the passage, so I'll leave it right there. Earlier the prophet said His breath is like a rushing torrent (Isaiah 30:28).
